resources.string: Start with a still, rigid, matte object with visible texture. Use even lighting. Glossy, transparent, moving or textureless surfaces may not reconstruct.

Take overlapping views while moving sideways around the object. Do not only rotate the phone in place. Include different heights while keeping the object still. Missing or unseen surfaces remain unknown.
Keep the same physical lens, zoom and aspect ratio. Avoid changing focus distance when possible. A guessed focal length is an assumption, not a measured lens calibration.

Inspect blurry, clipped or poorly overlapping photographs and retake them when needed. Current sparse analysis accepts up to twelve photographs and depth uses up to eight registered views. More photographs do not automatically mean a complete object.

The included board has 9 × 6 inner corners in a 10 × 7 square pattern. Print it flat without cropping. Photograph the full board at varied positions and tilts using the same optics as the object. The current workflow requires 10–40 board photographs. Lens calibration alone does not establish metric object scale.

Points, open surfaces and photograph-textured triangles are different outputs. Holes and seams can remain. Scale is arbitrary unless tied to a real known-distance reference. The app cannot measure unseen surfaces or guarantee watertight, print-ready geometry.

Capture, reconstruction and viewing work locally without an account or app networking. Originals stay in private app storage. Uninstalling removes them. Export important originals and results first. A document provider you choose may have its own cloud behavior.
Calibration checkerboard, 9 by 6 inner corners. Print the included SVG asset at its original aspect ratio.
